facts.title: An Egyptian Surgical Manual Is Over 3,500 Years Old
facts.summary: The Edwin Smith Papyrus, copied around 1600 BC, is the oldest known surgical treatise on trauma, explaining how to examine, diagnose and treat injuries.

facts.title: Bread and Beer Were Ancient Egypt's Staple Foods
facts.summary: Ancient Egyptians grew emmer wheat, barley and other cereals and used them to make their two staple foods: bread and beer.

facts.title: Cleopatra Lived Closer to the Moon Landing Than to the Pyramids
facts.summary: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid of Giza.

facts.title: Cleopatra's First Language Was Greek, Not Egyptian
facts.summary: Cleopatra's first language was Koine Greek, yet she was the only Ptolemaic ruler known to have learned Egyptian.

facts.title: Egypt Became a Roman Province After Cleopatra
facts.summary: After Cleopatra's death in 30 BC, Egypt became a province of the Roman Empire, ending the Hellenistic period that had begun with Alexander the Great's death in 323 BC.

facts.title: Egyptian Women Could Own Property and Divorce
facts.summary: In ancient Egypt, women as well as men could own and sell property, make contracts, marry and divorce, inherit and take disputes to court.

facts.title: It Took 23 Years to Crack Hieroglyphs
facts.summary: The Rosetta Stone was found in July 1799, but it took until 1822 for Jean-François Champollion to announce how the Egyptian scripts could be read.

facts.title: Napoleon's Soldiers Didn't Shoot Off the Sphinx's Nose
facts.summary: The Great Sphinx's nose was not shot off by Napoleon's soldiers; it was missing long before the French army reached Egypt in 1798.

facts.title: The Great Pyramid Took About 26 Years to Build
facts.summary: The Great Pyramid of Giza, built as the tomb of the pharaoh Khufu around 2600 BC, took about 26 years to complete.

facts.title: The Rosetta Stone Has Left the British Museum Only Once in Peacetime
facts.summary: Apart from wartime, the Rosetta Stone has left the British Museum only once: for one month in October 1972, when it was shown at the Louvre in Paris.

facts.title: The Rosetta Stone Says the Same Thing Three Times
facts.summary: The Rosetta Stone carries one decree from 196 BC written three ways: in Egyptian hieroglyphs, in Demotic script and in Ancient Greek.

facts.title: The Rosetta Stone Was Found by French Soldiers
facts.summary: French army officer Pierre-François Bouchard found the Rosetta Stone in July 1799, during Napoleon's invasion of Egypt, in the wall of a fort.

facts.title: Tutankhamun's Tomb Was Found Almost Intact in 1922
facts.summary: Howard Carter found the tomb of Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings in November 1922.
